raw_case_text:
A 78 yr old man from a rural area at the western of Iran referred to Razi Hospital Dermatology Clinic, Tehran for multiple ulcerative and exudative lesions on mid face, dorsal aspect of hands and the posterior aspect of heels (Fig. 1, 2).
Informed consent was taken from the patient.
Lesions initiated three years before with papules on the dorsal aspect of the hands then progressively enlarged above the upper lip, anterior portion of the nasal fossa, above the eyebrows and heels and became ulcerative.
During the past 3 yr, the lesions of hands were so developed that destroyed the tendons and soft tissue of fifth finger in the right hand so led to amputation of this finger. There was no history of comorbid condition, drug consumption, systemic symptoms, weight loss, fever, lymphadenopathy, hepatosplenomegaly or any signs of systemic involvement in physical examination and laboratory survey.
Multiple treatments in order to some heterogenic diagnosis such as pyoderma gangrenosum, sarcoidosis, and leishmaniasis were tried without any improvement in lesions.
In Razi Hospital Dermatology Clinic, initial Skin biopsy revealed necrotizing and palisading granulomatous tissue pattern that suggested infections etiology but the smear of lesions for fungal and mycobacteria and Leishmania was negative. In order to result of PPD test with 27 mm induration, anti-tuberculosis treatment including isoniazid, rifampin, ethambutol, and pyrazinamide was started.
A month after initiating drugs for tuberculosis, the smear of leishmaniasis repeated that was positive this time, the second biopsy revealed pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia and infiltration of the dermis by mixed inflammatory cells and Leishman bodies compatible with leishmaniasis.
Restriction fragment length polymorphism (RFLP) PCR was carried out on DNA extraction was carried out with QIAGEN Kit according to the manufacturer's instruction using two primers, LITSR (5-GTG CAG GAT CAT TTT CCG ATG) and L5.8s: 5-TGA TAC CAC TTA TCG CAC TT was designed for LTS1-PCR and cutting with and HaeIII enzyme. Positive controls containing DNA of L. major, L. tropica and a negative control containing distilled water were included. The PCR-RFLP on specimens of lesions proved L. major as the pathogenic agent (Fig. 3).
From the left side, the 2 bands show L. major, the second 2 bands show L. tropica, the 5th one is the specimens of lesions that compatibles with L. major and the last one show L. tropica.
Treatment initiated with 3 gr per day of meglumine antimoniate (Glucantime ) until 1 wk followed by 4.5 gr per day for another week, in spite of good response to meglumine antimoniate after 2 wk of treatment we forced to discontinue of drug because of cardiac toxicity (Figs. 4, 5).
The patient was informed about publishing his figures whit covering eyes.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 78-year-old male presented with a 3-year history of multiple ulcerative and exudative lesions on his mid-face, dorsal hands, and heels.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient presented with chronic skin lesions that started 3 years earlier as papules on the dorsum of both hands, which progressively enlarged and ulcerated over the upper lip, anterior nasal fossa, eyebrows, and posterior heels. The hand lesions progressively destroyed tendons and soft tissue of the right fifth digit, leading to its amputation. Prior empiric therapies for presumed pyoderma gangrenosum, sarcoidosis, and leishmaniasis had failed. At the dermatology clinic, an initial skin biopsy showed necrotizing granulomatous inflammation, but initial smears were negative; due to a positive PPD test (27 mm induration), anti-tuberculosis therapy (isoniazid, rifampin, ethambutol, pyrazinamide) was initiated for 1 month without improvement. Repeat smear and biopsy were subsequently performed.
subjective.past_medical_history: No comorbid chronic conditions; prior amputation of right fifth digit due to soft tissue and tendon destruction from skin lesions. Epidemiological exposure: resident of a rural area in western Iran.
subjective.review_of_systems: Denies fever, weight loss, or systemic symptoms. Home medications: anti-tuberculosis therapy for 1 month prior to admission. Allergies: None documented.

objective.physical_examination: Dermatologic examination revealed multiple ulcerative and exudative lesions over the mid-face (above upper lip, anterior nasal fossa, above eyebrows), dorsal aspect of both hands, and posterior aspect of heels. Right fifth finger was amputated. No peripheral lymphadenopathy, hepatosplenomegaly, or signs of systemic involvement.
objective.routine_investigations: Tuberculin skin test (PPD): 27 mm induration. Routine laboratory survey: normal with no signs of systemic involvement.
objective.advanced_workup: Initial skin biopsy: necrotizing and palisading granulomatous tissue pattern; initial lesion smears negative for fungi, mycobacteria. Second skin biopsy: pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia and dermal infiltration by mixed inflammatory cells.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Cutaneous leishmaniasis caused by Leishmania major.
Diagnostic confirmation: Repeat lesion smear demonstrated Leishmania amastigotes; second skin biopsy revealed dermal infiltration with mixed inflammatory cells and Leishman bodies; PCR-RFLP analysis targeting ITS1 (primers LITSR and L5.8s, digested with HaeIII) confirmed Leishmania major as the etiologic agent.
Differentials ruled out: Cutaneous tuberculosis (unresponsive to 1 month of 4-drug anti-TB therapy; mycobacterial smear negative), pyoderma gangrenosum, sarcoidosis, and deep fungal infections (fungal smear negative).
Treatment and clinical course: Initiated on meglumine antimoniate (Glucantime) at 3 g/day for 1 week, increased to 4.5 g/day for the second week with favorable lesion regression. However, therapy was discontinued after 2 weeks due to cardiotoxicity.
